recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit. Further core edits for FHIR-28490 would duplicate existing guidance or risk conflicting with later applied decisions; any future changes should be handled as separate Subscription filter issues.
issue_request: FHIR-28490 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked to clarify which criteria or filters apply to which qualifying resources between Subscription.filterBy and SubscriptionTopic resourceTrigger/canFilterBy. The proposal added a 0..1 resource discriminator to Subscription.filterBy, made SubscriptionTopic resource triggers repeat with a single resource each, and moved canFilterBy under the resource-specific trigger.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been initially applied by git commit 4f3fcec0394f15c2c0a93f377b15fd0b866b3c9f, whose body includes 'First pass of FHIR#28490' and which changed Subscription examples plus Subscription and SubscriptionTopic spreadsheet sources. The current XML resource definitions are later build/refactor outputs of that model rather than the original spreadsheet representation.
additional_context: Later final decisions explain the differences between the 2020 Jira wording and current source: FHIR-30383 clarified filter evaluation across multiple resource triggers, FHIR-39033 retained the resource discriminator and added framework guidance, FHIR-41197 renamed Subscription.filterBy.resourceType to Subscription.filterBy.resource, and FHIR-46492 collapsed SubscriptionTopic.resourceTrigger/eventTrigger into the current repeating SubscriptionTopic.trigger with canFilterBy under trigger.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Active current-build source has Subscription.filterBy.resource as 0..1, points it at SubscriptionTopic.trigger.canFilterBy.resource, defines SubscriptionTopic.trigger as repeating with a single resource, and includes framework/resource-page narrative explaining multi-resource topics and resource-qualified filters.
